headline: Would have funded six areas of the federal government for fiscal year 2024 and extended several health, family, and Pacific island programs.
what_it_does: This bill would have combined 6 of the 12 yearly spending bills for 2024, covering military construction, veterans, agriculture and food safety, commerce and justice, energy and water, the environment and public lands, and transportation and housing. It would have set many rules on how agencies could spend that money. It also would have extended several health and family programs through late 2024 and approved updated agreements with Micronesia, the Marshall Islands, and Palau.

who_it_affects.how: Would have funded VA health care and benefits, required the VA to phase out using Social Security numbers to verify identity, allowed fertility treatment for some disabled veterans, and barred reporting certain veterans to the gun background check system without a court finding that they are dangerous.
Would have paid for base construction, family housing, barracks, and planning for child care centers.

who_it_affects.group: Families who use food assistance like SNAP and WIC
who_it_affects.how: Would have funded these nutrition programs and school meal programs, kept current school sodium limits through the 2026-2027 school year, and allowed flavored milk in school meals.
Would have permanently required states to cover medication treatment for opioid addiction and would have kept people from losing Medicaid or CHIP coverage while in jail or prison, starting in 2026.

who_it_affects.group: Doctors and hospitals that treat Medicare patients
who_it_affects.how: Would have raised some doctor payments in 2024 and extended extra payments for small rural and low-volume hospitals through 2024.
Would have extended TANF cash assistance and child welfare programs.
Would have funded housing vouchers, public housing, and homeless assistance grants.
Would have extended funding for community health centers and the National Health Service Corps through December 31, 2024.

who_it_affects.group: Citizens of Micronesia, the Marshall Islands, and Palau
who_it_affects.how: Would have approved new aid agreements and let those living legally in the U.S. get federal means-tested benefits without the usual five-year wait.

who_it_affects.group: Medical marijuana patients and businesses in states where it is legal
who_it_affects.how: Would have barred the Justice Department from using its funds to block those state medical marijuana laws.
